items.old: .autocomplete-list, .autocomplete-optgroup, .autocomplete-optgroup-label, and the check icon's .icon inside an option
items.appliesWhen: You wrote a global rule against `.ds-overlay-pane .autocomplete-list` or a sibling. Nothing to do if you only use the `<ds-autocomplete>` element and its inputs.
items.pitfall: The panel is portaled to document.body, so these rules are almost always global rather than component-scoped — grep your global stylesheets, not just the component next to the picker.
items.verify: The autocomplete's open panel carries `ds-dropdown-panel` on its `.cdk-overlay-pane`, and its rows have 4px padding and a 4px radius without any rule of yours.
items.note: The panel now renders through the same shared partial as ds-select and ds-multi-select, so it inherits their padding, row radius, selected-row hooks and pressed states. An override that existed only to close that gap is dead weight, and one that names an old class silently stops matching.
items.action: Retarget every rule that names an old class, then delete the ones that only restored padding or row radius.

items.pitfall: The old token painted BOTH the hover and the selected row, because the autocomplete had no separate selected treatment. The panel-level hooks separate them, so a single old value may need splitting across two.
items.verify: Retuning --ds-option-selected-bg-color repaints the autocomplete's selected row, which it did not before.
items.note: The autocomplete had no separate selected treatment, so one token painted both hover and selection. The panel-level hooks reach all three pickers and separate the two states, which is what the 0.9.0 notes already claimed was true.

items.old: A settled single value wider than the trigger wrapped onto a second line and pushed the chevron onto a third — measured 40px to 63px at a 144px trigger.
items.appliesWhen: You use `<ds-autocomplete>` in single mode in a narrow column.
items.pitfall: Multi mode is unchanged — its chips already had a measured cap. This only affects the settled single value.
items.verify: A long value in a 144px-wide single-select autocomplete keeps the trigger one row tall and ends in an ellipsis, with the full text on the element's title.
items.note: A settled single value now clips with an ellipsis and keeps the trigger one row tall, with the full text on the element title. Multi mode is untouched — its chips already had a measured cap. Nothing in your markup has to change unless the wrapping was deliberate.
items.action: Do nothing, or set valueOverflow="wrap" on the pickers that relied on the value wrapping.

items.old: class MySelect extends SelectComponent, class MyMultiSelect extends MultiSelectComponent
items.appliesWhen: Subclassing a DS component is unsupported, but consumers do it. Template users of the `<ds-…>` elements need nothing.
items.pitfall: `protected` is no protection: a redeclared protected member collides exactly as a public one does.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS2415 or TS2416 naming a picker component.
items.note: ds-select and ds-multi-select gained a `width` input, and ds-select gained a private `panelTokens` field. Subclassing a DS component is unsupported but consumers do it, and a redeclared member collides whether it is public or protected. The compiler enumerates every collision, so a build is the whole check.
items.action: Build after upgrading; rename or `override` any member of yours that collides with `width` or `panelTokens`.

items.pitfall: Only a declaration that re-declares the type structurally (rather than importing it) could notice, and it still sees the same union.
items.verify: The app builds and `width` still accepts only 'fill' and 'content'.
items.note: AutocompleteWidth is now an alias of the shared DsControlWidth that SelectWidth and MultiSelectWidth also alias. The union it resolves to is unchanged, so an import keeps compiling and `width` still accepts exactly `fill` and `content`.

informational: ds-multi-select and ds-select gained `width`, the input ds-autocomplete already had: `content` takes the trigger width as the panel's floor instead of its width, so a short trigger stops forcing an unreadable panel. Default `fill` is unchanged.
New panel bounds for that mode: --ds-dropdown-panel-minw and --ds-dropdown-panel-maxw.
ds-select now forwards its panel custom properties onto the portaled pane, which it never did — a `ds-select { --ds-dropdown-panel-*: … }` reaches the panel now instead of being silently dropped.

deleteList.why: The autocomplete panel shipped with `padding: 0` and square rows while ds-select's dropdown had `--space-1` padding and rounded rows, so consumers patched the difference globally. The panel now uses the same shared partial as the other two pickers and matches without help.
deleteList.replaceWith: Nothing — delete the rule. The padding is --space-1 and the row radius is --ds-radius-inner out of the box; --ds-dropdown-panel-minw / -maxw are there if you want to bound the panel.
